newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cricket-NZ test win a statistician's delight.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-NZ test win a statistician's delight.

text.p: LAHORE, Nov 25 - New Zealand's victory in the first cricket test against Pakistan at Gaddafi Stadium flooded statisticians with new data, NZPA reports.
Among the many records established in the game were:

* The most leg before wicket decisions given in a test match in Pakistan. The 15 lbw dismissals beat the previous record on Pakistani soil of 14 awarded when the home side played Sri Lanka in Faisalabad in the 1991-92 season. The world record remains the 17 lbws granted in 1993 when Pakistan played the West Indies in Port of Spain, Trinidad.

* Mohammad Wasim, 19, scored a brilliant 109 not out in the second innings to become just the fourth Pakistani batsman to make a century on debut. He joins Billy Ibadulla, Javed Miandad and Salim Malik.
* Pakistani legspinner Mushtaq Ahmed took career-best match figures of 10 for 143, beating the 10 for 171 he captured against New Zealand in Christchurch one year ago.
* Simon Doull earned test-best match figures of eight for 85, including a personal best of five for 46 in Pakistan's first innings.
* Stephen Fleming attained his highest score in tests, 92 not out. His previous best was 92, scored on debt against India in the 1993-94 season.

* Mark Greatbatch contributed just one run in the tourists' second innings but it was enough to raise his 2000th test run in 40 appearances. He joins a group of 14 New Zealanders to have reached the landmark.

* Lee Germon becomes only the second New Zealand captain to win a test in Pakistan. The only other skipper to do that was fellow Cantabrian Graham Dowling, whose 1969 team won by five wickets on the same ground on their way to an historic 1-0 series win.
* Sydney import Steve Rixon wins at his first outing as New Zealand coach.
* It was just New Zealand's fifth test win in 38 tests against Pakistan.
